newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean won ends lower on strong dollar/yen.
newsitem.headline: South Korean won ends lower on strong dollar/yen.

text.p: The South Korean won ended Monday trading lower against the dollar, pressured by the U.S. unit's firmness against the Japanese yen, brokers said.
The won ended at 849.60 against an opening of 849.50. It moved in a 849.40-849.80 range during the day.
"We expected the dollar to test the 850 level today because of its strength against the yen, but worries that the central bank would intervene were too strong to overcome," said a local bank dealer.
The dollar touched a 46-month high of 117.67 in early trading in Tokyo.

Dealers said Tuesday's won/dollar movement would hinge on the dollar/yen rate. "If the dollar/yen rate remains at around 117, the dollar could test 850 won. But the volume of import and export deals will play a major factor," said another local dealer.
The base mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 849.70 on Tuesday, compared to Monday's 848.80.

The domestic currency has also been undermined by fears that of a widening trade deficit after major export industries were disrupted by nation-wide strikes in protest at the passage of a controversial labour law.
